narrative.overview:
The page behaves like a market panel at the opening bell: a clock, a pulsing "ao vivo" status, and rows of tabular serif numerals. Warmth comes from an ivory canvas and printed-feeling serif headlines; energy comes from whole sections flooded in lime or ink rather than from cards, gradients, or ornament. The reader moves ivory, lime, ink, ivory, lime, ink, so each section change is a hard color change of the entire band.

Density is generous (sections 72-128px of vertical padding, 1180px content column), but inside a section the content is typographic: big serif numerals, ruled lists, italic serif quotes. Structure is drawn with 2px ink rules and 1px warm lines, not boxes.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed color fields: lime, ink, ivory and warm surface bands.
Roboto Serif at 600 for every heading and numeral, italic serif for the turn word and quotes; Roboto for everything functional.
Photography of Bruno cut out on a lime block, bleeding to the viewport edge in the hero.
Flat surfaces; one soft shadow, only on screenshots in /obrigado.
Motion limited to highlighter sweep, live-dot ping, button lift, FAQ plus rotation; all off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Text-Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime is a field or a fill on ivory; as text it is Lime Ink on light grounds and Bright Lime on ink. Signal Lime never colors text.

rules.name: The Whole-Band Rule
rules.body: Color changes happen at section edges as full-width bands. Do not tint half a section or float a colored card to fake a change of field; the exceptions are the three recorded panels (plan, fit-yes, testimonial highlights).

rules.name: The Serif Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every figure a visitor compares (price, hours, counts, clock) is Roboto Serif 600 with lining-nums tabular-nums.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Italic serif is for the turn word of a heading and for quoted speech; nothing else is italic.

rules.name: The Flat-Field Rule
rules.body: Panels are separated by color or rule, never by shadow; the one shadow stays on screenshots.

dos: Do switch whole sections between ivory, lime and ink, and set text per ground: Floor Ink on lime, Canvas Ivory on ink.
Do use Lime Ink for lime-family text on light grounds and Bright Lime on ink.
Do set prices, times and counts in Roboto Serif 600 with tabular lining numerals.
Do draw structure with 2px ink rules and 1px Warm Line dividers.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion (all animation and transition off) and keep the focus outline per ground.
donts: Don't put Signal Lime on text over ivory; contrast fails.
Don't add shadows to panels or cards.
Don't replace testimonials with a carousel or the sections with icon-card grids.
Don't introduce a third family or a system display face; Roboto Serif and Roboto only.
